concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time such as O(n log n).

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Expressions Σ c_k y^k with coefficients, added and multiplied term by term.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with i² = −1, with modulus and unit-modulus phases e^{iθ}.

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine reading and writing cells of one or more tapes, moving each head one cell per step.

concepts.name: Fixed finite-tape Turing machine model
concepts.gloss: The complexity model of the paper: one machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, where time counts single-cell steps and fixed extra tracks only change time by a constant factor.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.
Fixed tracks and finitely many work tapes change time by a fixed factor.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's 1971 O(n log n log log n) multitape multiplication, with their proposal that n log n is the optimal growth order; Harvey and van der Hoeven later reached O(n log n), and the paper refutes optimality of n log n in this model.

evidence.quote: and proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier (Harvey–van der Hoeven)
concepts.gloss: The known fixed-tape integer multiplication algorithm running in O(N log N) on N-bit inputs, used by the paper only as an ordinary subroutine on shorter records.

evidence.quote: Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Arrays as tape streams and elementary scans
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in lexicographic order on tape with implicit addresses; logical volume V is the number of stored bits, and digit moves, digit-pair permutations, splitting on a digit and cyclic row splitting into W streams all take O(V) steps with counters included.

evidence.quote: An address is implicit in an entry's position in this ordered stream
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts and rational scalings
concepts.gloss: In O(V) steps a target address field can be cyclically shifted by an offset computed from earlier control fields, or multiplied by a fixed unit modulo q^b, by splitting each fiber into pieces and merging them in another order.

evidence.quote: The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Linear maps, rank, projections and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: Invertible linear operators and matrices, rank, subspaces with a bilinear form, projection onto a nondegenerate subspace along its orthogonal complement, and the same ideas over the two-element field.

evidence.quote: choose an invertible linear operator
Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution and the discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The normalized DFT F_q turns cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication (F(u*v) = q·Fu·Fv), and the opposite-sign transform inverts it up to scaling.

evidence.quote: cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups

concepts.name: Multidimensional (tensor) transforms
concepts.gloss: A transform over several axes is the tensor product of one-dimensional transforms, applied line by line along each axis; convolution on a product of cyclic groups is computed by it.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two

concepts.name: Multiplication as convolution of radix digits
concepts.gloss: Writing each n-bit input as a polynomial in 2^b with b-bit digits, the integer product is the convolution of the digit lists followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder axis map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism sending x to a product of x_i^{μ_i} turns one cyclic convolution of length S = s_1⋯s_d (pairwise coprime) into a convolution on d prime-length axes; it is realized by padded layouts and triangular controlled shifts.

evidence.quote: theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution
First, the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution.

concepts.name: Two-point butterfly and decimation-in-frequency layer
concepts.gloss: The map (u,v) → ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2) applied on pairs of entries; the radix-2 FFT recursion pairs z_k with z_{k+t/2}, applies this butterfly, multiplies by a twiddle, and recurses on the two halves.

evidence.quote: decimation-in-frequency step pairs
simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: The Harvey–van der Hoeven technique that expresses a Fourier transform of prime length s through a transform of the larger power-of-two length t via Gaussian-weighted maps, up to a small controlled error.

evidence.quote: The Gaussian resampling argument uses two maps
Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: A DFT-like sum is rewritten using the product of two chirp phases so that it becomes a pointwise phase multiplication, a cyclic convolution with a fixed chirp array, and another phase multiplication.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
The chirp identity below performs the frequency change

concepts.name: Resampling with the permutations left in the transform
concepts.gloss: Instead of sorting the data twice per coordinate, the source and target coordinate permutations are kept in the transform formula, the middle transform becomes a chirp convolution, and the source permutation cancels across two forward transforms, their pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.
Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The polynomial indeterminate, whose powers act as roots of unity by signed shifts of the coefficient list.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree less than r with y^r = −1, where multiplying by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list and so acts as a cheap root of unity.

evidence.quote: is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two.

concepts.name: Phase twist from cyclic to negacyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by e^{πik/r} maps cyclic convolution of length r isomorphically onto convolution modulo y^r + 1, and the inverse twist recovers the cyclic result with the correct wrap sign.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms (Nussbaumer)
concepts.gloss: Normalized DFTs over the polynomial ring whose roots of unity ω_t = y^{2r/t} are signed coefficient shifts, so the radix-2 butterfly levels need no general multiplications; they are contractions and invertible up to scaling.

evidence.quote: multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list
The ring has zero divisors, so we verify character cancellation

concepts.name: Fixed-point grids, truncation and contraction error bounds
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers stored with p fractional bits in the unit disk, truncation toward zero to the grid costing less than √2·2^{-p} per step, and linear contractions propagating errors without growth so errors of composed steps add.

evidence.quote: A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it.
A $p$-bit grid array has real and imaginary coefficient parts in $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$.

concepts.name: Restoring arbitrary scratch values
concepts.gloss: A linear schedule of eight rows (subtract old side and center contributions, copy, gather, scatter, side-inject, undo) that adds the wanted update to a target and returns every scratch wire to its arbitrary initial value.

evidence.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation in
For arbitrary initial values of its auxiliary wires, a forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value unchanged.

concepts.name: Three-element subset gadget
concepts.gloss: Indexing data by three-element subsets of {1..100}, gather and scatter through central wires create coefficients depending on intersection size and side wires on neighboring triples cancel the unwanted ones, leaving exactly y_S ← y_S + x_S.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, and

concepts.name: Three-stage bank exchange network
concepts.gloss: Applying the forward invocation at stage 1, its inverse at stage 2 and the forward invocation at stage 3 sends (X,Y) to (−Y,X) with every scratch wire restored; the bit version is a pure exchange using XOR gates, the complex version uses Gaussian dyadic values.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

concepts.name: Frames: changing representation along the network
concepts.gloss: An invertible linear operator D_v attached to each source, gate and sink: the stored array is D_v applied to the logical array, an edge applies D_vD_u^{-1}, and since the gate is pointwise linear the common frame commutes with it, so intermediate frames cancel and only endpoint frames matter.

evidence.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and
Thus the intermediate frames cancel, and a route from input role $w$ to output

concepts.name: Nested subspace labels and orthogonal residuals
concepts.gloss: Each gate and terminal gets a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space, adjacent labels are nested, and an edge's orthogonal residual (the complement of the smaller label in the larger) has dimension equal to the change in label dimension; the gadget's triple lines are chosen so the total dimension lost stays small.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
The subspaces at adjacent vertices are nested.

concepts.name: Strict total rank deficit s < W·m
concepts.gloss: The sum s of edge ranks (bit network) or residual dimensions (complex network) over a network with W wires and m-dimensional labels is strictly less than W·m, so the number of smaller recursive calls per wire is below m.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
We will obtain $L<N/2$.

concepts.name: Lower-triangular (Bruhat) factorization of a matrix
concepts.gloss: Every rational m×m matrix A of rank a factors as E₁ΠE₂ with E₁, E₂ invertible lower triangular and Π a partial permutation with exactly a ones, so a shear by A costs exactly a interchanges plus linear-cost triangular updates in tape order.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Bit network as an address shear
concepts.gloss: With frames given by shears Φ_M that map address (H,D) to (H+MD,D), the bit network's endpoint operator on every role is the shear H ← H+D, and each edge costs as many smaller interchanges as its rational rank.

evidence.quote: For the bit procedure, that endpoint operator is an address shear:
two fields, written as vectors $H,D$ over a common residue ring, are updated by $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$.

concepts.name: Role streams and fixed-tape depth-first scheduling
concepts.gloss: Rows are distributed cyclically among the W wire roles so each recursive child works on one stream of volume V/W with the same local address set, and the recursion runs depth-first on a fixed number of tapes using a parking stack for inactive streams.

evidence.quote: Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count for each prefix to a multiple of $W$.
Reserve $W$ role tapes, a fixed set of I/O and elementary-operation work tapes, one parking stack tape, and a separate descriptor stack.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving from s/W < m
concepts.gloss: A call on parameter m·f makes s calls on parameter f over volume V/W each, so normalized cost satisfies F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1) with s/W < m, which sums to O(m^{kτ}) for some τ < 1.

evidence.quote: This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.
F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The first tape procedure: two disjoint u-bit address chunks of a bit array are swapped in O(V·u^τ) time for a fixed τ < 1, by the shear D←D−H, H←H+D, D←H−D where the middle shear is done by the bit network recursively, with padding to supply rows and handling arbitrary widths.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product. Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.
Although its final effect is an exact permutation, its intermediate steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition with guard repair
concepts.gloss: A binary row addition on the same selected bit in many K-bit chunks at once, done by a constant number of whole-chunk cyclic shifts (eight rotations) plus chunk swaps, then a deterministic sort-based repair of the exponentially small set of addresses whose guard values are too close to the segment ends.

evidence.quote: We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two address chunks.
Those changes are implemented by whole-chunk moves and controlled shifts, followed by a deterministic correction of the explicitly identified exceptional addresses.

concepts.name: Phase-frame (complex) network for the butterfly
concepts.gloss: The complex bank-exchange network with binary labels and frames C_U = H^{⊗m} diag(i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4}) H^{⊗m}, in which an edge's frame change is a product of two-point kernels aI + bX_v, one per residual basis vector, and the endpoint operator is the tensor power C^{⊗m} of the kernel C = H·diag(1,i)·H.

evidence.quote: For the numerical procedure, the endpoint operator becomes the simultaneous $H_0$ layer after diagonal phase operations and a dyadic scale.
Use the complex scalar network and binary labels.

concepts.name: Recursive implementation of the phase network on selected bits
concepts.gloss: A group of e = m·f selected axes is split into m slots of f chunks; basis changes by invertible binary matrices (products of row additions) and one child call of C^{⊗f} per residual basis vector implement each edge, giving s child calls each on volume V/W, and H₀^{⊗D} = b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D converts the result to a normalized layer.

evidence.quote: Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.
We first construct tensor products of the auxiliary two-point kernel

concepts.name: Exact Gaussian dyadic arithmetic and guard widths
concepts.gloss: The whole accelerated layer is computed exactly on Gaussian dyadics with explicit extra integer and fractional guard bits (growing like d^20 = o(p)), so only one truncation to the p-bit grid is applied after the completed contractive layer.

evidence.quote: The accelerated network is evaluated exactly until an entire normalized butterfly layer is complete.
Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics, whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer in O(V·d^λ′)
concepts.gloss: The second tape procedure: applying H₀ at the same bit offset in up to d equal-width address chunks of polynomial records at once, with one truncation, in time O(V·d^λ′) for a fixed λ′ < 1 rather than d separate passes.

evidence.quote: one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$ equal-width address chunks, and the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.
whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

concepts.name: Transform layout and retained frequency order
concepts.gloss: The d−1 transform axes are rearranged by single-bit moves and width-K chunk exchanges so that each round's selected bits lie at a common offset in consecutive chunks; the forward transform outputs frequencies in a fixed permuted order that the pointwise product and the opposite transform consume without unpermuting.

evidence.quote: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands.
The forward procedure may retain its output layout for a pointwise product and the following opposite procedure.

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution) for ring products
concepts.gloss: Real and imaginary parts of two polynomial records are evaluated at B = 2^{4p} as signed integers, multiplied with the established multiplier, and the coefficients recovered by centered residues and reduced modulo y^r + 1, in time O(rp log(rp)).

evidence.quote: The reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution
Four exact integer products dominate the linear packing, extraction, combination, wrapping, and truncation costs.

concepts.name: Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Two forward synthetic transforms in retained order, M pointwise polynomial products by signed packing, and the opposite transform compute convolution divided by T over the remaining axes with polynomial-ring values, with error O(M·ℓ·2^{-p}) and cost O(Tp[dK + pK^{τ−1} + ℓd^{λ′} + log(rp)]).

evidence.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order.
Convolution from the retained transform layout

concepts.name: Complex cyclic convolution by a coefficient twist
concepts.gloss: Cyclic convolution over all d scalar axes is computed by twisting the last axis into the polynomial ring, convolving the other d−1 axes with ring convolution, and untwisting, with disk-margin and error accounting.

evidence.quote: The power-of-two complex convolution used in the chirp identity is obtained from the synthetic convolution by a coefficient twist.

concepts.name: Prime source lengths near the powers of two
concepts.gloss: Distinct odd primes s_i in ((1−2η)t_i, (1−η)t_i] are found by deterministic scanning so that their product exceeds T/2 and each ratio t_i/s_i leaves the separation Gaussian resampling needs.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two $t_i$

concepts.name: Padded power-of-two box and linewise tensor maps
concepts.gloss: Source arrays live in the full padded box of T entries; a one-dimensional map is applied to each line of an exposed axis in turn, with axis exposure and restoration by adjacent chunk interchanges costing O(Tp d²(1+ℓ^τ)).

evidence.quote: For the tensor product, apply the one-dimensional maps to one coordinate line at a time.

concepts.name: Source transform: compress, chirp convolution, expand
concepts.gloss: The procedure that computes the permuted prime-length transform of a tensor of digits: linewise expansion by the Gaussian map, the chirp transform via complex convolution, linewise compression, and an exact scaling by 2^γ.

evidence.quote: apply the linewise approximation to $\mathcal A$, apply the computed chirp transform

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carry propagation
concepts.gloss: The computed convolution has error below 1/2 per coefficient, so rounding gives the exact integer digit-convolution coefficients, which are bounded by 2^{3b} and turned into the binary product by radix carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order.
Round the represented real values to the nearest integers.

concepts.name: Parameter choices and the cost table giving κ
concepts.gloss: Fixed rational exponents (τ = 1 − 2^-50, ε = 2^-75, c = 2^-56, λ′ = 1 − 2^-54, δ = 1/16, …) and sizes p = 6⌈log₂n⌉, d ≈ p^ε, T ≈ n/b, r = 2^ℓ make every normalized cost term at most p^{1−2κ}, giving total time O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) with κ = 2^{-182}.

evidence.quote: Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.
These constants are deliberately conservative; no optimization is claimed.

concepts.name: The assembled multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Split inputs into b-bit digits, place them by the Chinese-remainder map, compute two source transforms, multiply pointwise, apply the opposite-sign source transform with the S-scalings that undo the normalizations, round, unmap, and propagate carries to output the 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain source arrays $u,v$.
The two occurrences of $S$ in this algorithm undo different normalizations.

concepts.name: Power-saving integer multiplication
concepts.gloss: The main theorem: one deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) time with κ = 2^{-182}, disproving the n log n optimality conjecture in this model, by combining the fast address interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers (each saving a power of the chunk width) with Gaussian resampling, chirps and synthetic polynomial transforms.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine $A$, with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, that computes this exact product for every $n\ge1$ and every pair of $n$-bit inputs.
We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time, with

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: The base-2 and natural logarithms and their identities, used for bit lengths, the lg n notation, and for treating exponents like (lg n)^{1-kappa} or 2^{-p} as growing or shrinking functions.

concepts.name: Floor, ceiling and rounding
concepts.gloss: The functions giving the greatest integer at most x, the least integer at least x, and the nearest integer to x, used for lengths such as ceil(log2 n) and for rounding computed values to integers.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: An integer written as a string of digits in radix 2 (or any radix b) with the leftmost digit most significant, so val(x) = sum x_i 2^{n-i}, with padding by leading zeros to a fixed length.

concepts.name: Schoolbook arithmetic and carries
concepts.gloss: The elementary algorithms for adding and multiplying integers digit by digit with carries, taking linear time for addition and quadratic time for multiplication.

concepts.name: Bitwise operations and XOR
concepts.gloss: Logical operations on bits, in particular exclusive or, which is addition modulo 2 and is its own inverse.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and residues
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo m, where a is congruent to b mod m when m divides a-b, with addition, multiplication and inverses of numbers coprime to m.

concepts.name: Primes, divisibility and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Divisibility of integers, prime numbers, the gcd and the Euclidean algorithm (including its extended form giving modular inverses), and the meaning of coprime and pairwise coprime integers.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The complex numbers w with w^t = 1, namely e^{2 pi i k/t}, which are the unit-modulus complex numbers whose powers cycle with period t.

concepts.name: Complex modulus, conjugate and triangle inequality
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
concepts.gloss: The modulus |z| = sqrt(a^2+b^2) of a complex number, its real and imaginary parts, and the inequality |u+v| <= |u|+|v| used to bound sums of errors.

concepts.name: Max norm and error bounds
concepts.gloss: The norm of a vector as its largest coordinate in absolute value, used to state that every coordinate of a computed array is within a stated error of the true one.

concepts.name: Little-o, big-Omega and Theta notation
concepts.gloss: The companions of big-O notation: f = o(g) when f/g tends to 0, f = Omega(g) for a lower bound, and Theta for matching upper and lower bounds.

concepts.name: Series and exponential decay estimates
concepts.gloss: Sums of geometric series and similar convergent series, and the fact that quantities like 2^{-p} are negligible against any fixed polynomial in the relevant size, used to sum recursive costs and bound errors.

concepts.name: Recurrences and recursion
concepts.gloss: Defining a procedure by calls to itself on smaller inputs, analyzing its cost by a recurrence such as F_k <= a F_{k-1} + c, and proving bounds by induction.

concepts.name: Sorting and stacks
concepts.gloss: Rearranging records into a prescribed order by comparison or by key, and the stack data structure with push and pop, used for depth-first recursion.

concepts.name: Sets, subsets and counting
concepts.gloss: Finite sets, subsets of a given size, intersections, Cartesian products of sets, binomial coefficients and the indicator (0/1) vector of a subset.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: A bijective rearrangement of a finite index set, its inverse, and the corresponding permutation matrix that reorders the entries of a list.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order and mixed-radix indices
concepts.gloss: Ordering tuples by comparing coordinates left to right, and storing a multidimensional array as a flat list so that a tuple (i_1,...,i_d) is at position sum i_j times the product of later axis lengths.

concepts.name: Matrices, matrix-vector products and inverses
concepts.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers acting on vectors by multiplication, with the identity, inverses of invertible matrices, and diagonal and triangular matrices.

concepts.name: Kronecker product of matrices
concepts.gloss: The block matrix A (x) B formed from two matrices, which acts on tensor-product index sets and satisfies (A (x) B)(C (x) D) = AC (x) BD.

concepts.name: Hadamard matrix and the 2x2 butterfly matrix
concepts.gloss: The 2x2 matrix with rows (1,1) and (1,-1) (up to scaling), whose tensor powers act on bit-indexed arrays, together with the 2x2 swap matrix with rows (0,1) and (1,0).

concepts.name: Inner products, orthogonality and eigenvalues
concepts.gloss: The dot product of vectors, orthogonality when it vanishes, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix as scalars and directions it only scales.

concepts.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
aliases: evaluate a polynomial at a point
concepts.gloss: Evaluating a polynomial at a value (in particular at a power of 2 to read it as an integer), and the idea that a polynomial of degree < N is determined by its values at N points.

concepts.name: Fixed-point and floating-point numbers
concepts.gloss: Representing real numbers as integers divided by a power of two (dyadic rationals), so p fractional bits give a grid of spacing 2^{-p} to which values are truncated or rounded, with rounding error below the spacing.

concepts.name: Karatsuba and the history of fast multiplication
concepts.gloss: The fact that integer multiplication can be done faster than the schoolbook quadratic time, so that the cost M(n) of multiplying n-bit integers is a nontrivial function studied in complexity theory.

concepts.name: Square roots and quotient with remainder
concepts.gloss: Division with remainder a = bq + r with 0 <= r < b, and the integer square root floor(sqrt(a)).

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (sets, functions, combinatorial counting, induction, basic modular arithmetic and number theory such as primes, gcd and the Euclidean algorithm), recursion and elementary algorithms (sorting, stacks, divide and conquer), basic Turing machines with several tapes, and the first-year mathematics that goes with it: single-variable calculus (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals, geometric series), matrices and vectors, polynomials and complex numbers. The reader has not met the discrete Fourier transform or the FFT, abstract algebra beyond modular arithmetic (rings, quotient rings, algebra isomorphisms, cyclic-group structure), Gaussian integers, number-theoretic results on the density of primes, or any integer-multiplication algorithm faster than the schoolbook method.
